segments.he: אחד מאנ"ש כשהי' בביתו והי' רוצה לעשות התבודדות ולהתאנח בעת ההתבודדות בעת שכבו על מטתו כמו שמובא בשיחות הר"ן והי' מתבייש ומתיירא מזוגתו שלא תכעוס עליו ע"כ קשר את השינים שלו שתחשוב שהשינים שלו כואבים לו ואז יהא מותר לו להתאנח.
segments.en:
Reb Sendir of Terhovitsa — called by all "Reb Sendir the Great" — was one of the great members of our fellowship, and the extremity of his awe and his service of G-d is impossible to estimate in the mind. He founded the Terhovitsa fellowship — who were servants of Hashem of our fellowship so extraordinary that they went beyond the bounds of the human and it is impossible to estimate or describe at all the extremity of their self-stripping from physicality and their self-sacrifice in their service. They would go at the beginning of summer to the forests and fields, engaged day and night in hisbodedus. When they went out they would sing in the known melody: "The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not yet saved." The nature of their service and their burning passion is impossible to estimate. Reb Sendir their leader had been previously a simple man — and once as a young man he threw a shoe at his mother who had rebuked him. But afterward when he drew close to Rabbainu's Chassidus and became greatly inflamed for the service of Hashem, he would be in the forests and mountains and fields day and night in hisbodedus and prayer without cease — eighteen hours — in melodies that broke the heart, such that whoever heard him, even the most wicked, became a complete ba'al teshuvah. When he would cry out at the holy grave in Uman, he could be heard from one end of the city to the other. Once the Rav of Tcheryn and other great members of our fellowship were traveling, and their route went through the forests of Terhovitsa. They heard a voice and followed the voice until they felt literally the stripping away of physicality from the sweetness of the voice. They saw it was Reb Sendir — still in the forests — and he was crying out: "I hate those who observe worthless vanities — but as for me, I trust in Hashem!" saying it to himself: "Zog, Sendir: 'Sanas hashomrim havlei shav — va'ani el Hashem vatakhti!'" And the Rav of Tcheryn said to the others with him: "It seems we must already be ashamed before him." "Es hot azoy ponim az mir meygn zikh shoyn shemen far im." And Reb Avraham would travel to Reb Sendir on Shabbos to see his service and receive from him.

Once on Erev Rosh HaShanah Reb Sendir encountered one of our fellowship who was a great miser. After they came out from the holy grave, Reb Sendir spoke with him about charity — speaking words of arousal with his characteristic burning passion — until the miser was so moved by the very power of his words that he took out his entire wallet with all his coins and gave it to Reb Sendir to distribute as charity. And the following year on Erev Rosh HaShanah, when they again came out from the holy grave, Reb Sendir wanted to approach him to speak with him — and the miser began to cry out loudly: "He is coming to rob me again!" "Er geyt mikh shoyn barebn!" For he knew that if Reb Sendir approached him and spoke with him, it would be impossible for him not to give him his entire wallet again — and therefore he gave himself this strategy: simply not to let him approach at all.
